entities.summary:
Cristoforo Solari, also known as il Gobbo, was an Italian sculptor and architect who created the iconic facade of the Pazzi Palace in Florence, Italy, in 1492. His brother, Andrea Solari, was a prominent painter of the High Renaissance.

Solari's work was influenced by the Classical orders of ancient Greece and Rome, which were revived during the Renaissance.

His legacy can be seen in the many buildings and monuments he designed and constructed, including the Duomo in Florence, which he worked on until his death in 1527.

The artist's life and work were marked by a series of significant events, including the Pazzi conspiracy of 1478, which led to the exile of the Solari family from Florence.

Despite the challenges he faced, Solari continued to work tirelessly, producing some of the most iconic and enduring works of the Renaissance.

In his later years, Solari became known as 'il Gobbo' or 'the Fool', due to his eccentric behavior and his tendency to be seen as a troublemaker by his contemporaries.

This nickname has endured, and Solari remains one of the most fascinating and enigmatic figures of the Renaissance.

Cristoforo Solari was born in 1470 in Florence, Italy, and died in 1527. He was a member of the Solari family, a prominent family of artists and architects in Florence during the Renaissance.


Cristoforo Solari was a key figure in the development of Renaissance architecture, and his work had a profound impact on the design of buildings and monuments throughout Europe.

Cristoforo Solari's legacy extends beyond his own work, as he helped to revive the study and appreciation of classical Greek and Roman architecture.


Cristoforo Solari's life and work are a testament to the enduring power of art and architecture to shape and transform human culture.


Cristoforo Solari's story is a reminder that even the most seemingly minor figures can have a profound impact on the course of history.
